messages.content: I am Oren. I have six plant pots on the flat roof of my building. I went up to water them and found the wind had rearranged the empty pots.
What do you do when a wind makes your empty pots behave?
The roof has a proper railing and a stair door. I am sitting safely by the door, feeling outnumbered by terracotta.
You have more of them than I have ever been able to arrange.
Three pots have beans. The others are marigolds, mint and one stubborn tomato plant.
I will put the number back in when you finish speaking.
Do you grow anything that is more trouble than it is worth?
The one I water most carefully has become a little too comfortable. It has very large leaves and an impressive flower. I like it for that, but it still needs to be fed.
My neighbour lent me a red watering can with a cracked handle. I keep forgetting to hold it underneath.
The broken handle does not seem to have forgotten anything about water.
I ought to return it and buy one, but I have grown rather fond of its terrible handle.
That can be difficult. A tool with a history is harder to replace.
Is there an object you keep using after it really ought to have been replaced?
My garden fork has become stubborn about returning to the garden. I remember it once when I was hurrying down the path. I was disappointed to have to wait for it.
The mint is thriving. Everything else seems to be negotiating with me.
That is a good report. I have not watered my three empty pots.
I can smell somebody downstairs frying onions. That is making my gardening enthusiasm evaporate.
You have been invited to supper.
What would you eat if nobody else had a say in supper tonight?
I like lentils. If I had to choose something now, I would choose lentils.
Yesterday I promised a bean plant to my niece. She wanted to know how long before it was taller than she was.
I would let her have the promise. I would also make a small bowl of lentils for her in the meantime.
I said I would ask the bean and get back to her. She thought that was a poor answer.
A clever bean might be impatient with that.
Were you patient with growing things when you were young?
I liked knowing where a seed would grow. I could move it out of the way to put in another seed. I was not always pleased with the final plant.
I was impatient with almost everything at that age. I still dig up seeds sometimes to see if anything is happening.
That is a small experiment. I like experiments that reveal something about a seed.
The stair door keeps catching on a little stone. I have moved it twice and the wind has brought it back.
You have a much better arrangement of stones than I have ever tried.
I am heading down shortly. Tell me about a small job you are putting off.
I have not finished the job I started. I am being polite to the wind instead of finishing it.
